overview: Two levels of surface-area-increasing folding in the small intestine, one visible to the naked eye and the other only under an electron microscope.
genZNote: Villi: the intestine's finger-like carpet. Microvilli: the even tinier hairs on top of each of those fingers.

aspects.label: Size and Visibility
aspects.valueA: Finger-like projections visible with a light microscope, roughly 0.5-1.5 mm long.
aspects.valueB: Microscopic projections on the surface of villi cells, visible only under an electron microscope.

aspects.label: Structural Level
aspects.valueA: Folds of the intestinal mucosa (multicellular structure).
aspects.valueB: Extensions of the plasma membrane of a single intestinal epithelial cell.

aspects.label: Combined Structure
aspects.valueA: Collection of villi covering the intestinal lining.
aspects.valueB: Microvilli on villi cells together form the 'brush border'.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Villi and microvilli together massively amplify the small intestine's absorptive surface area — often cited as increasing it several hundred-fold.
overlay.memoryTrick: Villi = visible finger-like folds. Microvilli = the microscopic 'brush border' hairs on each villus cell.
overlay.commonMisconception: Microvilli are not simply smaller versions of villi at the same structural level — they exist one level down, as membrane extensions of individual cells that make up each villus.
